name: National City
seo_title: Christmas Events for Kids in National City, CA 2026
seo_desc: Kids' Christmas in National City, CA: A Kimball Holiday tree lighting, snow sledding, Santa at Plaza Bonita and the historic National City Depot.
lede: National City does Christmas in Kimball Park, where the city's A Kimball Holiday brings a tree lighting, snow-hill sledding, train rides and Santa, with more Santa visits at the library and Plaza Bonita.
celebrates: The big night is A Kimball Holiday, a free, family-friendly celebration the City of National City throws in Kimball Park next to City Hall. Families ride a free train, slide down a snow hill, write letters to Santa and dance on an LED dance floor while community groups perform on stage. Santa, Mrs. Claus and the Grinch pose for photos, and the crowd counts down together to the tree lighting at 6 pm. The National City Public Library turns into Whoville for an afternoon of Santa photos, music, crafts and cookie decorating, and Plaza Bonita hosts Santa at Center Court, including a quiet sensory-friendly morning.
lastyear: In 2025 the city held its 17th Annual A Kimball Holiday on Saturday, December 13, from 2 to 8 pm in Kimball Park on E 12th Street. The tree lighting ceremony started at 6 pm. The city promised free train rides, snow-hill sledding, letters to Santa, a live DJ, stage performances and photos with Santa, Mrs. Claus and the Grinch. Because A Avenue closed for the day, the city asked visitors to take public transit or park on D Avenue or at the library.
facts: National City is the second oldest city in San Diego County. It was incorporated on September 17, 1887, on land that was once part of the 26,000-acre El Rancho de la Nacion. Frank Kimball and his brothers Warren and Levi bought the rancho in 1868, cleared land, built roads and the city's first wharf, and brought the railroad to town. That is why the Christmas celebration in the park is called A Kimball Holiday.
trains: National City has real railroad history. The National City Depot, built in 1882 for the California Southern Railway, was the first terminus of transcontinental rail travel in the San Diego area and is the oldest railroad building still standing in San Diego County. The city restored it in 1998, and the San Diego Electric Railway Association runs it as a museum on weekends. BNSF freight trains still pass nearby. From the San Diego Trolley, take the Blue Line to the National City / 24th St station, about four blocks from the Depot.

faq: It is the City of National City's yearly holiday celebration in Kimball Park on E 12th Street. In 2025 the city described it as a free, family-friendly event with train rides, snow-hill sledding, letters to Santa, a live DJ, stage performances, photos with Santa, Mrs. Claus and the Grinch, and a tree lighting ceremony at 6 pm.
Where should I park for A Kimball Holiday?

In 2025 the city closed A Avenue between National City Boulevard and 12th Street, including the City Hall lot, so parking was limited. It suggested public transit or the Kimball Park stalls on D Avenue and the National City Public Library lot at 1401 National City Boulevard.
Is there a sensory-friendly Santa in National City?

Yes. Plaza Bonita, at 3030 Plaza Bonita Road, offers a Sensory-Friendly Santa Experience before the mall opens, with reduced noise and holiday coloring. The visit with Santa is free and photo packages are optional. Reservations are strongly recommended, and walk-ins are welcome as space allows.
Can kids see old trains in National City?

Yes. The National City Depot at 922 W 23rd Street is an 1882 railroad station run as a museum by the San Diego Electric Railway Association. It is open Saturdays and Sundays from 10 am to 4 pm and closed on Christmas. Freight trains still pass the building.
How do I get to National City by trolley?

The San Diego Trolley Blue Line runs through National City. The National City / 24th St station is about four blocks east of the National City Depot, which makes the trolley an easy way to combine a train ride with a visit to the old station.
